newsitem.title: USA: Exxon Chinese power venture moves ahead.
newsitem.headline: Exxon Chinese power venture moves ahead.

text.p: Exxon Corp said Thursday Exxon Energy Ltd and China Energy Investment Co Ltd have signed the joint venture agreement for the development of a 1,050 megawatt natural gas-fired power plant project in Shenzhen, north of Hong Kong.

China Energy Investment is a subsidiary of China Light & Power Co Ltd, which has been in a joint venture with Exxon Energy in the power generation business in Hong Kong for more than 30 years. The Shenzhen project represents an extension of the two companies' cooperation outside Hong Kong.

Under the agreement, which has been cleared by the Ministry of Electric Power in Beijing, Exxon Energy and China Energy Investment will each have a 17.5 percent interest in the project. Shenzhen Qianwan Electric Power Development Co Ltd and Guangdong Electric Power Holding Co, both People's Republic of China government corporations, will have a combined 36 percent interest and Kanematsu Power (South China) Co Ltd will have a 29 percent interest.

Exxon noted the parties signed a memorandum of understanding in October 1996 for the project which will consist of three units of 350 megawatt class combined cycle gas turbines, with natural gas as the main source of fuel.
The plant is expected to become operational by the end of the century, the company said.

Castle Peak Power Co Ltd, which is owned 60 percent by Exxon and 40 percent by China Light & Power, has engaged in discussions with the project consortium regarding the supply of natural gas to the project under a long-term contract from the Yacheng 13-1 field in the South China Sea, owned by China National Offshore Oil, Kuwait Petroleum and Atlantic Richfield Co, the operator.
